items.title: Invoice OCR API for Logistics Expense Tracking Automation
items.snippet: Logistics and transportation companies handle large volumes of invoices for fuel, freight, tolls, and vendor services. Manually recording these expenses can slow down financial tracking and increase the chances of data entry errors. An Invoice OCR API helps automate this process by extracting important information directly from invoice images or PDFs. Using OCR technology, the system can capture details such as invoice numbers, vendor names, dates, line items, and total amounts. This structured data allows businesses to monitor logistics expenses more efficiently, simplify reconciliation, and improve overall financial visibility across transportation operations.

items.title: Invoice OCR API for Automated GST Data Extraction in India
items.snippet: Invoice processing and GST data management can be time-consuming when handled manually. An Invoice OCR API helps automate this process by extracting important information directly from invoice images or PDFs. Using AI-powered OCR technology, the system can detect fields such as invoice number, vendor details, invoice date, line items, and total amounts. It can also capture GST-specific data like GSTIN numbers, HSN/SAC codes, taxable values, and tax amounts. Automating invoice data extraction helps businesses reduce manual entry errors, speed up reconciliation, and simplify GST compliance when handling large volumes of invoices. https://azapi.ai/blog/invoice-ocr-api-with-gst-extraction-india/

items.title: FinCrew: Multi-Agent AI Financial Intelligence
items.snippet: SMBs and mid-market companies ($10M-$200M revenue) spend 40-60% of finance time on manual data entry, invoice management and basic reconciliation. Existing solutions don't serve the mid-market segment. They're either SMB-focused or enterprise-only. We're targeting the $150B+ TAM in between. We're looking for feedback, beta users, and discussing investment. Happy to answer questions in the thread.

items.title: Tell HN: AI coding is sexy, but accounting is the real low-hanging target
items.snippet: Working on automating small business finance (bookkeeping, reconciliation, basic reporting). One thing I keep noticing: compared to programming, accounting often looks like the more automatable problem: It’s rule-based Double entry, charts of accounts, tax rules, materiality thresholds. For most day-to-day transactions you’re not inventing new logic, you’re applying existing rules. It’s verifiable The books either balance or they don’t. Ledgers either reconcile or they don’t. There’s almost always a “ground truth” to compare against (bank feeds, statements, prior periods). It’s boring and repetitive Same vendors, same categories, same patterns every month. items.title: Desvincular a linha pix do Mercado Pago que completa uma forçada parcial de PIX
items.snippet: ## O que falta Na forçada parcial de PIX (#92), o resto do pagamento pode vir de um PIX recebido do banco ou da linha pix do Mercado Pago (conciliação de cartão). O PR da #92 recusa desvincular o PIX do banco que completa uma forçada parcial ("desfaça a forçada antes"). Desvincular a linha pix do Mercado Pago da venda ainda não tem a mesma trava: a linha forçada ficaria marcada como recebida sem o dinheiro que a completava. ## O que fazer - Aplicar ao desvincular da conciliação de cartão a mesma regra do PIX: recusar só a linha que completa a forçada parcial, com a mesma frase, e permitir desfazer a forçada no mesmo lugar. - Teste de banco com a venda de moto, a OS e a venda de peça.
